evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/main.rs:119-143 `cors_layer()` (PRODUCTION) and backend/servers/api-server/src/lib.rs:463-488 (inside `create_router`, the INTEGRATION-TEST router per its own doc comment at lib.rs:440-451) build TWO separate, divergent CorsLayers. The codebase deliberately unified router/middleware into a single source (`route_table()`, issue #867; security_headers mirrored #963) precisely to stop test-vs-prod drift — but CORS is the one middleware left NOT unified, and it has already drifted on two axes.

AXIS 1 — allow_headers (the dangerous one): the TEST router (lib.rs:479-485) allows `x-tenant-id` in allow_headers; the PRODUCTION layer (main.rs:133-140) does NOT list `x-tenant-id`. Tenant-scoped api-server routes require the `X-Tenant-ID` header (RlsConnection extractor), and the browser SPA ppt-web sends it cross-origin: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/routes/groups/rentals.tsx:200 returns `{ Authorization, 'X-Tenant-ID': auth.xTenantId }` and the shared `authenticatedFetch` client (#3000) attaches it; the generated api-client (frontend/packages/api-client/src/generated/types.gen.ts, many endpoints) carries `X-Tenant-ID`. With `allow_credentials(true)` set on BOTH layers and `https://ppt.three-two-bit.com`/`https://reality.three-two-bit.com` in the allowed-origin list, a cross-origin browser request carrying `X-Tenant-ID` triggers a CORS preflight that PRODUCTION rejects (header not in allow_headers) while the integration tests (which run `create_router`, where the header IS allowed) pass green — a prod-only preflight failure on every tenant-scoped browser call, masked by the divergent test config.

AXIS 2 — origins: production `get_cors_allowed_origins()` (main.rs:69-100) honors the `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` env var (comma-split, validated, with fallback); the test router hardwires `parse_default_origins()` (lib.rs:110-115) and ignores the env entirely. So the entire production CORS override path (env parsing, the 'set but all-invalid -> fallback' branch) is NEVER exercised by any integration test — a regression there ships undetected.

VERIFICATION FOR IMPLEMENTER: confirm the prod topology — if ppt-web/reality-web reach the api-server CROSS-ORIGIN in production (the allowed-origins list and allow_credentials(true) strongly imply yes), AXIS 1 is an ACTIVE prod bug (tenant-scoped browser requests fail preflight); if all browser traffic is same-origin/reverse-proxied so no preflight fires, it is a latent gap. Either way AXIS 1+2 are a real test/prod divergence. FIX: extract ONE shared `cors_layer()` (env-aware, with the full allow_headers set incl. `x-tenant-id`) into the shared build path the way route_table()/security_headers were unified under #867/#963, have both main.rs and lib.rs::create_router consume it, and add a guard test (mirroring `route_table_is_single_source_of_truth`) so the CORS config can never silently diverge again.

backend/servers/api-server/src/lib.rs:100-108 `DEFAULT_CORS_ORIGINS` = [http://localhost:3000, http://localhost:3001, http://localhost:8080, http://localhost:8081, https://ppt.three-two-bit.com, https://reality.three-two-bit.com]. This list is the PRODUCTION fallback: main.rs:69 `get_cors_allowed_origins()` returns `parse_default_origins()` whenever `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` is unset OR set-but-no-valid-entries (main.rs:85-99). Combined with `allow_credentials(true)` (main.rs:141), a production deploy that forgets to set `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` silently trusts four `http://localhost:*` dev origins as credentialed CORS origins.

Trusting plaintext `http://localhost:*` origins with credentials in a production CORS allowlist is a latent misconfiguration (dev origins should never be trusted by a prod edge; it also widens the surface for local-attacker / malicious-dev-tooling scenarios). The failure is silent — the only signal is an info-level `tracing::info!("CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS not set, using default origins")` at main.rs:95, easy to miss.

FIX: split the default origin set by environment — localhost origins only when RUST_ENV=development (the same gate totp.rs/main.rs use for dev fallbacks), and in production either require `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` to be set explicitly (fail-fast panic with an actionable message, matching the JWT_SECRET pattern at main.rs:539-547) or fall back to prod-only origins (the two three-two-bit.com entries) with no localhost. Low risk, backend-only, statically landable.
